title: "14 Methodological case report or series"
link-citations: true

Alternative labels: 

## Definition and features 
In a methodological case report, a team describes their experience with the design, implementation, or performance of a method in a real study, typically their own. In a case series, they discuss two or more studies that share a similar method or methodological challenge.

::: {.callout-tip appearance="minimal" collapse="true"}
## Boundaries with related types
[Experimental analysis of real datasets](3real-datasets.qmd): may also use a single dataset and the label “case study” but re-analyze an existing dataset to answer a methodological question.

[Informal approaches](15informal.qmd): may also refer to a “cases" to illustrate methods.

[Review of applied methods](9review-applied.qmd): While a case series is narrative, a review of applied methods answers specific research questions. 
:::

## Typical purposes and corresponding examples 
[Evaluate a single method](../purposes/7evaluate-method.qmd): Experience with using large language models to develop a clinical practice guideline;[@SousaPinto2024ai] Lessons learned from applying a framework to develop a healthcare intervention;[@Lindblom2025navigating] Challenges and benefits of including non-randomized evidence in living systematic reviews;[@Bonnet2026including] Demonstration of target trial emulation.[@Martinuka2023target]
